notes.title: Splatterbot - Update v1.02
notes.content:
Added keyboard support for Player 1
 Fixed UI issues in 21:9 aspect ratios.
 Fixed bug where Splatterbots would stop painting when paintballs were spawned.
 Fixed bug where Splatterbots would stop painting when respawning on water levels.
 Alleviated issues with AI getting stuck (they still struggle a little on the conveyor belts but I'm working on it!)

notes.title: Splatterbot is Available Now!
notes.content:
Greetings all, 

Today is the day. after almost 3 years Splatterbot is finally here! 

I'm so excited to share Splatterbot with the world. I hope that everybody has as much fun playing Splatterbot with their friends and family as I do with mine.  

To celebrate the launch, we have a 10% launch discount on Steam. We've also partnered with Turtle Flip Studio to create the Splatellite bundle featuring both Splatterbot and Which Way Up: Galaxy Games at a discount.

Thank you all so much for your support throughout development — your encouragement has meant the world to us. The future of Splatterbot is looking bright, but now it's time to jump in and make some mess with your friends and family!  

- Nathan

notes.title: Splatterbot - Dev Update #3
notes.content:
Hey Everyone!

Splatterbot is a part of the Couch Co-op Fest on Steam. To celebrate, we have released an update to the demo with Team Mode! 

Team Mode is similar to the base FFA mode, except there are only two colours available. Players can compete in 2v2 or 3v1 - with other players or bots!

Please note that a controller is required to play Splatterbot.

As a general development update - Development is coming along nicely. The Nintendo Switch version is is coming along nicely. The team mode has been implemented - as seen in the demo. At the moment I'm focusing on polish and bug fixes - particularly related to the user interface. I've got some fun concepts lined up for new game modes, levels and power-ups for post-launch content but I have to keep those tucked away for now to get Splatterbot to you all in the next few months! :)

notes.title: Splatterbot - Dev Update #2
notes.content:
Steam Next Fest has begun! and we have some important update news to share!

First for the bad news - we have had to delay Splatterbot's release date. The main reason for this is a delay in Nintendo Switch development. Splatterbot is now scheduled to launch on Steam and Nintendo Switch simultaneously in early 2025.

The good news is, our demo is now available for Steam Next Fest! If you're itching to play, you can check out our Splatterbot Demo on our Steam Store page: Splatterbot

Please note that a controller is required to play Splatterbot.

notes.title: Splatterbot - Dev Update #1
notes.content:
Hi, I'm Nathan - the sole developer of Splatterbot. I've been hard at work on Splatterbot for the past year and a half, and I want to give some development updates in the leadup to launch.

A few days ago, I released an updated trailer. I recently overhauled the environments and added character customization, so I wanted to showcase these in the new trailer. You can watch it below:

[previewyoutube=OWyQwteJ0rU;full][/previewyoutube]

In the near future, my number one priority is getting a demo ready in time for Next-Fest. Tweaking the gameplay based on feedback, improving the UI, and getting a Steam Deck version ready are my #1 priority in the next few months.

If you want to stay posted, add Splatterbot to your wishlist!

- Nathan
